source: AAA gasprices.aaa.com national average — Memorial Day Monday print $4.507 (Day 87, May 25, 2026). AAA landing page banner: 'Memorial Day Weekend Gas Prices Reach Four-Year Highs.' +50.7% above $2.99 Feb 28 baseline; ~$1.40/gal above year-ago levels; ~10¢ below the June 2022 all-time record of $4.61; eased ~4¢ over three weeks from the May 7 print of $4.55. State extremes May 25: California ~$6.116; Hawaii $5.641; Washington D.C. $4.661; Oklahoma ~$3.98. Patrick De Haan (GasBuddy) attributes 'more than 90%' of the YoY increase directly to the Iran war. CNN/SSRS poll (April 30–May 4, n=1,499, ±2.8pp; CNN Politics May 12): 21% approve Trump on gas prices, 75% say the Iran war has had a negative effect on their finances. Watson Institute / Costs of War (Brown — Jeff Colgan, May 2026): cumulative extra fuel costs to U.S. consumers since war start now top $40 billion, more than $300 per household. Memorial Day Monday cash markets closed; oil futures fell ~5–6% intraday on US–Iran deal optimism (WTI ~$91, Brent ~$94.82 intraday low — 'lowest since April 2026') following the Rubio 'framework 95% there' framing and Trump's 5–7 day deadline. Pump-price relief, if a deal lands, runs 2-3 weeks behind crude per De Haan. Rep. Thomas Massie (R-KY) on NBC Meet the Press May 24: 'Gas is almost $5 a gallon, diesel is almost $6 a gallon, and the farmers here in Kentucky can't afford the fertilizer to put on their fields.'
